name: Mir
dispatch: Mir was the first modular space station — and the bridge between two eras of spaceflight. Where every station before it was launched whole, Mir was assembled in orbit over a decade, module by module, growing into a sprawling complex that stayed aloft for fifteen years. It set the endurance record that still stands (Valeri Polyakov's 437 unbroken days, proof a crew could survive a Mars-length flight), outlived the Soviet Union that built it by a decade, and survived a fire and a depressurising collision in 1997 that its crew fought off by hand. In its final years American Shuttles docked with it and US astronauts lived aboard — the rehearsal, in hardware and in trust, for the International Space Station that inherited nearly everything Mir worked out.
description: The first modular space station, assembled in orbit between 1986 and 1996 and continuously occupied for almost 10 years (1989–1999), with a final crew visit in April–June 2000. Hosted American astronauts during the Shuttle-Mir program (1995–1998) — the partnership that made ISS possible.
